title: UMN Signs at the Bedside — Babinski, Hoffmann, Clonus and the Jaw Jerk

hook.en: Four quick bedside signs separate a damaged brain or spinal cord from a damaged nerve. Learn to elicit each one safely and to say exactly what it means.
hook.ur: Chaar tez bedside signs kharab dimagh ya spinal cord ko kharab nerve se alag karte hain. Har ek ko mehfooz tareeqay se nikalna aur uska sahi matlab batana seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll elicit the plantar response, Hoffmann sign, ankle clonus and jaw jerk correctly, and use them to tell an upper motor neuron lesion from a lower motor neuron one.
goal.ur: End tak aap plantar response, Hoffmann sign, ankle clonus aur jaw jerk sahi nikalenge, aur unse upper motor neuron lesion ko lower motor neuron lesion se alag karenge.

text.en: The brain and spinal cord (the **upper motor neuron**, UMN) normally keep the spinal reflexes calm. When that pathway is damaged — stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, cervical myelopathy — the brake is cut and **primitive reflexes escape**: brisk tendon reflexes, **clonus**, an **upgoing big toe** (Babinski), **Hoffmann's sign**, increased tone (spasticity) and a pyramidal pattern of weakness. Finding two or more of these together is far more convincing than one.
text.ur: Dimagh aur spinal cord (**upper motor neuron**, UMN) normally spinal reflexes ko pur-sukoon rakhte hain. Jab yeh pathway kharab ho — stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, cervical myelopathy — to brake kat jati hai aur **primitive reflexes nikal aate hain**: brisk tendon reflexes, **clonus**, **upar uthta angootha** (Babinski), **Hoffmann sign**, barha hua tone (spasticity) aur kamzori ka pyramidal pattern. In mein se do ya zyada ka ek saath milna kisi ek se kahin zyada convincing hai.

text.en: A baby has an upgoing toe because the brain's wiring is not finished. In an adult with a UMN lesion, the wiring is cut and the "baby reflexes" return. Babinski is a throwback to infancy.
text.ur: Bachay ka angootha upar uthta hai kyunke dimagh ki wiring poori nahi hui. UMN lesion wale bade mein wiring kat jati hai aur “bachon wale reflexes” wapas aa jate hain. Babinski bachpan ki taraf wapsi hai.

intro.en: Watch the examiner stroke up the **outer edge of the sole and across the ball of the foot** with a blunt point. Use the **Response** buttons to compare the normal flexor response (toes curl down) with Babinski (great toe extends and the toes fan).
intro.ur: Dekhein examiner blunt point se **sole ke outer edge se upar aur ball of the foot ke across** stroke karta hai. **Response** buttons se normal flexor response (toes neeche mudti hain) ko Babinski (bara angootha extend aur toes phail jati hain) se compare karein.

text.en: Do not stroke so hard it hurts, and do not mistake a withdrawal for an upgoing toe. A ticklish patient pulls the whole foot away. Hold the ankle, use a blunt point (the end of a key or an orange stick) and stroke slowly. Also remember that the plantar response is unreliable in infants under about 1 year (upgoing is normal) and may be hard to read in a very ticklish or severely deformed foot.
text.ur: Itna zor se stroke na karein ke dard ho, aur foot khenchne ko upar uthta angootha na samjhein. Gudgudi wala patient poora foot kheench leta hai. Ankle ko pakrein, blunt point (key ka sira ya orange stick) use karein aur aahista stroke karein. Yeh bhi yaad rakhein ke takriban 1 saal se chhote bachon mein plantar response bharosay ka nahi (upar uthna normal hai) aur bohat gudgudi wale ya bigre hue foot mein parhna mushkil ho sakta hai.

question.en: On stroking the sole, the great toe extends and the other toes fan out. What does this show?
question.ur: Sole par stroke karne se bara angootha extend hota hai aur baqi toes phail jati hain. Yeh kya dikhata hai?

text.en: An upper motor neuron lesion (a positive Babinski sign)
text.ur: Upper motor neuron lesion (positive Babinski sign)

feedback.en: Yes — the extensor plantar response means the corticospinal pathway is damaged. Look for other UMN signs and refer if it is new.
feedback.ur: Haan — extensor plantar response ka matlab corticospinal pathway kharab hai. Doosre UMN signs dhoondein aur naya ho to refer karein.

feedback.en: Normal is the toes curling down (flexor response).
feedback.ur: Normal mein toes neeche mudti hain (flexor response).

feedback.en: LMN lesions give reduced reflexes and a flaccid foot, not an extensor plantar.
feedback.ur: LMN lesions mein reflexes kam aur foot dheela hota hai, extensor plantar nahi.

intro.en: The examiner holds the patient's middle finger loosely and **flicks the fingernail downwards**. Watch the thumb and index finger. Toggle **Positive** to see them flex together. A brisk positive suggests an upper motor neuron lesion above C8, such as cervical myelopathy.
intro.ur: Examiner patient ki middle finger ko dheelay se pakarta hai aur **nail ko neeche ki taraf flick** karta hai. Thumb aur index finger dekhein. **Positive** toggle karein to dono saath flex hoti dikhengi. Brisk positive C8 se upar upper motor neuron lesion batata hai, maslan cervical myelopathy.

title.en: Four UMN signs side by side

rows.en: Stroke the outer sole and across the ball of the foot
rows.ur: Sole ke outer edge aur ball of the foot ke across stroke
Bara angootha extend, toes phail jati hain

rows.en: Flick the nail of the relaxed middle finger
rows.ur: Relaxed middle finger ke nail ko flick
Thumb aur index saath flex hoti hain

rows.en: Support the knee slightly bent and sharply dorsiflex the foot, then hold
rows.ur: Knee halka bent rakh kar support karein, foot ko tezi se dorsiflex karein, phir hold

rows.en: More than 5 rhythmic beats while held (sustained)
rows.ur: Hold karne par 5 se zyada rhythmic beats (sustained)

rows.en: Finger on the chin, mouth slightly open, tap the finger downwards
rows.ur: Chin par finger, munh halka khula, finger par neeche tap

rows.en: A brisk jaw closing: lesion above the pons
rows.ur: Jaw ka tezi se band hona: pons se upar lesion

intro.en: Hold the knee slightly bent and sharply dorsiflex the foot. In the **Result** options compare "normal (0–2 beats)" with "sustained clonus". Count the rhythmic beats on screen.
intro.ur: Knee ko halka bent rakhein aur foot ko tezi se dorsiflex karein. **Result** options mein “normal (0–2 beats)” ko “sustained clonus” se compare karein. Screen par rhythmic beats ginein.

question.en: How many beats of ankle clonus are considered abnormal?
question.ur: Ankle clonus ki kitni beats abnormal maani jati hain?

text.en: More than about 5 beats, or beats that continue while the stretch is held
text.ur: Takriban 5 se zyada beats, ya jab tak stretch hold ho beats chalti rahein

feedback.en: Yes — one to three beats can be normal in a brisk, relaxed patient; sustained clonus is a UMN sign.
feedback.ur: Haan — brisk, relaxed patient mein ek se teen beats normal ho sakti hain; sustained clonus UMN sign hai.

feedback.en: A beat or two that die away is common and normal.
feedback.ur: Ek ya do beats jo khatam ho jayen aam aur normal hain.

text.en: Only when the patient feels pain
text.ur: Sirf jab patient ko dard ho

feedback.en: Clonus is rhythmic muscle contraction, not a pain response.
feedback.ur: Clonus rhythmic muscle contraction hai, dard ka response nahi.

text.en: **What to do with a UMN sign.** A new Babinski, clonus or Hoffmann in a patient with neck or back pain, clumsy hands, a changed gait or sphincter symptoms is a red flag for cervical myelopathy or cord compression — arrange urgent medical review. In a known stroke or SCI patient, the same signs are expected: document them and use them to plan tone management, positioning and stretching.
text.ur: **UMN sign ka kya karein.** Gardan ya kamar ke dard, anari haathon, badli hui gait ya sphincter symptoms wale patient mein naya Babinski, clonus ya Hoffmann cervical myelopathy ya cord compression ka red flag hai — urgent medical review ka intezam karein. Maaloom stroke ya SCI patient mein yehi signs expected hain: unhein document karein aur tone management, positioning aur stretching ke plan mein use karein.

text.en: In cervical myelopathy a **cluster** of findings is more useful than any single sign: gait deviation, a positive Hoffmann sign, inverted supinator sign, a positive Babinski and age over 45 together make the diagnosis far more likely. Hoffmann alone is only moderately sensitive and specific, and a mildly positive Hoffmann can occur in healthy people with brisk reflexes.
text.ur: Cervical myelopathy mein findings ka **cluster** kisi ek sign se zyada kaam ka hai: gait deviation, positive Hoffmann sign, inverted supinator sign, positive Babinski aur 45 saal se zyada umar saath mil kar tashkhees ko kahin zyada mumkin banate hain. Akela Hoffmann sirf moderately sensitive aur specific hai, aur halka positive Hoffmann brisk reflexes wale healthy logon mein ho sakta hai.

question.en: A patient's biceps jerk is absent, but their finger flexors jerk briskly when you tap the brachioradialis (the "inverted supinator sign"). What does it show?
question.ur: Patient ka biceps jerk gayab hai, lekin brachioradialis tap karne par finger flexors tezi se jhatka dete hain (“inverted supinator sign”). Yeh kya dikhata hai?

answer.en: A **cervical cord lesion at C5–C6**: the C5–C6 reflex arc itself is damaged (so the arm reflex is lost, the LMN part), while the levels below (the finger flexors, C8) are released (the UMN part). It helps you find the level of cervical myelopathy.
answer.ur: **C5–C6 par cervical cord lesion**: C5–C6 reflex arc khud kharab hai (is liye arm ka reflex gayab, LMN hissa), jabke neeche ke levels (finger flexors, C8) azad ho gaye (UMN hissa). Yeh cervical myelopathy ka level dhoondne mein madad deti hai.

question.en: Which combination points most clearly to an UMN lesion?
question.ur: Kaun sa combination UMN lesion ki taraf sab se wazeh ishara karta hai?

text.en: Brisk reflexes, sustained clonus, upgoing toe and spasticity
text.ur: Brisk reflexes, sustained clonus, upar uthta angootha aur spasticity

feedback.en: Yes — several UMN signs together are convincing.
feedback.ur: Haan — kayi UMN signs ka saath hona convincing hai.

text.en: Absent reflexes, wasted muscles and fasciculations
text.ur: Gayab reflexes, wasted muscles aur fasciculations

feedback.en: That is the lower motor neuron pattern.
feedback.ur: Yeh lower motor neuron pattern hai.

text.en: Reduced reflexes, weak muscles and glove-and-stocking numbness
text.ur: Kam reflexes, kamzor muscles aur glove-and-stocking numbness

feedback.en: That pattern fits a peripheral neuropathy.
feedback.ur: Yeh pattern peripheral neuropathy se milta hai.

text.en: **Refer urgently** if UMN signs are new, if they come with progressive weakness, bladder or bowel change, a band-like trunk sensation or severe neck pain after trauma. Do not manipulate or stretch the neck when UMN signs are present until a doctor has cleared the cord.
text.ur: **Foran refer karein** agar UMN signs naye hon, ya barhti kamzori, bladder ya bowel ki tabdeeli, dhar ke gird band jaisa ehsaas ya trauma ke baad gardan ka shadeed dard saath ho. UMN signs ho to jab tak doctor cord ko clear na kar de gardan ko manipulate ya stretch na karein.

summary.en: UMN lesions release primitive reflexes: brisk jerks, sustained clonus, extensor plantar (Babinski), Hoffmann and spasticity.
summary.ur: UMN lesions primitive reflexes ko azad kar dete hain: brisk jerks, sustained clonus, extensor plantar (Babinski), Hoffmann aur spasticity.

summary.en: Elicit each sign gently with correct technique; more than one sign together is far more convincing than a single sign.
summary.ur: Har sign ko sahi technique se aahista nikalein; ek se zyada signs ka saath hona kisi ek sign se kahin zyada convincing hai.

summary.en: A new UMN sign with neck or back symptoms, clumsy hands or sphincter change is an emergency; do not manipulate the neck.
summary.ur: Gardan ya kamar ke symptoms, anari haathon ya sphincter tabdeeli ke saath naya UMN sign emergency hai; gardan ko manipulate na karein.

front.en: What is a positive Babinski sign?

back.en: Extension of the great toe with fanning of the other toes on stroking the sole — an UMN sign (normal in infants).
back.ur: Sole par stroke karne se bare angootay ki extension aur baqi toes ka phailna — UMN sign (bachon mein normal).

front.en: How do you elicit Hoffmann's sign?

back.en: Hold the relaxed middle finger and flick the fingernail downwards; thumb and index finger flex together if positive.
back.ur: Relaxed middle finger ko pakar kar nail ko neeche flick karein; positive ho to thumb aur index saath flex hoti hain.

front.en: How many clonus beats are abnormal?
front.ur: Clonus ki kitni beats abnormal hain?

back.en: More than about 5 beats, or beats that continue while the stretch is held (sustained clonus).
back.ur: Takriban 5 se zyada beats, ya jab tak stretch hold ho beats chalti rahein (sustained clonus).

front.en: What does a brisk jaw jerk tell you?
front.ur: Brisk jaw jerk kya batata hai?

back.en: A lesion above the pons (bilateral UMN), since the jaw jerk arc passes through the pons (CN V).
back.ur: Pons se upar lesion (bilateral UMN), kyunke jaw jerk ka arc pons (CN V) se guzarta hai.

note.en: The full compare-and-contrast of upper and lower motor neuron signs.
note.ur: Upper aur lower motor neuron signs ka mukammal muqabla.
